text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak gave another warning about the troubles in the peace process because of obstacles placed by the government of Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel. He told The New York Times that the general climate in the area had become very bad because of Netanyahu reneging on the Oslo agreements signed by the Palestinians and the Israelis.

- At a meeting to review the outcome of the Middle East economic conference, Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said that President Mubarak's view of the conference proved right. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said the prime minister decided to set up a working group of businessmen to list the projects which were submitted during the conference and which met a response, to make proposals about marketing them and to publicise other projects until they reach contract stage.

- Safwat el-Sherif said a ministerial meeting agreed to complete measures for a tender on November 25 for the canal in the Western Desert. By the end of December the Ministry of Public Works should have awarded the contract and work on digging the first two km (one mile) of the canal should start in the first week of January. An international tender for the pumping stations should be called by the end of December.

- Floods and rain in Red Sea province have knocked down or damaged 250 houses in the town of Hurghada and one person died by electrocution. Work in some government departments has stopped and everyday life is completely paralysed.
- The supreme administrative court ruled yesterday that only the People's Assembly (parliament) is qualified to examine challenges to the results of the 1995 elections.

- President Mubarak announced that the aim of giant projects in Egypt is to raise the living standards of the people. He said that Arab and Israeli public opinion is the cornerstone for correcting the course of the peace process.

- The Israeli businessmen who took part in the Cairo economic conference said in Alexandria that they were giving Prime Minister Netanyahu one week's grace to solve the problem of Hebron and warned that the consequences for the Israeli economy would be grave if the peace process stops.
- Zagazig University has found a royal Pharaonic tomb at Tell Basta in the Nile Delta. The tomb contains a mummified body with a covering of gold and reliefs on the walls.

- Many parts of the south have had rain, floods and thunderstorms. More than 280 families have lost their homes, one person was killed in Hurghada and the airports at Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh have been closed.
- A ministerial meeting decided on immediate measures towards digging the new canal in the Western Desert.
- A Japanese government report on the investment climate in Egypt indicates constant improvement and rising growth rates.

- The Israeli spy Azam Azam, confronted with the Egyptian spy Emadeddin Abdelhamid Ismail, confessed to spying for Mossad and giving Ismail special equipment for gathering information and economic statistics.
- USAID head John Westley said the level of U.S. aid to Egypt in 1997 would be the same as it was this year.
